tool_input.command: git stash -q && bun test 2>&1 | tail -8 && git stash pop -q

result: The bug was a one-character off-by-one in `PostController.index`: it validated `page` with `ListPostsQuerySchema` (which already defaults to `1` and enforces `min(1)`, i.e. the query string is 1-based), then passed `page + 1` to the ORM's 1-based `paginate()`, so every request rendered the page after the one asked for — `/posts` and `?page=1` both showed rows 11–20, and the newest ten posts were unreachable. I changed `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:16` to pass `page` through unchanged; since the paginator derives its meta (`currentPage`, `from`/`to`, `lastPage`) and first/last/prev/next links from the ORM result's `currentPage`, that single change also fixes the pager's highlighted page and the "from–to of total" numbers, with ordering, page size, and search untouched. I also added a `posts.index pagination` suite to `tests/PostController.test.ts` that inserts 25 posts, drives the Inertia response for `/posts`, `?page=1`, and `?page=2`, and asserts page 1 is the ten newest ids, page 2 the next ten, and that every post appears exactly once across the whole pager (with an `afterAll` that removes the rows it created so the persistent test SQLite file isn't grown by each run); those three tests fail against the old `page + 1` code and pass now, and both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (5 pass, 0 fail) are green.
